category_title: Jamaican Grade 7 students with multiple literacy failures who transition from 'at-risk' to 'risk-takers' through radio simulation
student_description: This Grade 7 student reads at a pre-primer level and masks deep discouragement from repeated literacy failures with a 'nonchalant, failure-proofed' attitude. However, they are highly capable when traditional literacy demands are replaced with oral-first, authentic role-play. They uniquely require literacy to be scaffolded through simulated radio broadcasting (listening and speaking first) to bypass their trauma around standardized testing.

criteria.rationale: Sustaining the radio station metaphor across all subjects provides a permanent, safe center of interest that keeps the student engaged over weeks and months.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly applies the radio/broadcast simulation to multiple core subject areas beyond just isolated literacy lessons.

criteria.rationale: Traditional standardized assessments trigger severe emotional distress and resistance, so progress must be measured through authentic social practices.
criteria.check: The long-term plan replaces traditional standardized testing with performance-based, conversational, or role-play milestones to assess student progress.
